verdict.rationale: Proa components are written in ordinary typed Rust (proa-docs-7, proa-docs-32), with markup inside a compile-time-validated template macro (proa-gh-2) and regular stylesheets that hot-apply (proa-docs-5, proa-docs-8). That suggests developers reuse familiar Rust, markup and CSS. However, nothing shows the template syntax is standard HTML rather than a custom DSL. Developers must also learn framework-specific concepts such as macros, md! templates, signals, RSJS islands and WebContext (proa-gh-3, proa-docs-16, proa-docs-18, proa-docs-26). Missing for 10: documentation showing templates use plain HTML/CSS syntax, evidence the concept count is minimal, hands-on learning-curve reports, and accessibility for developers who don't already know Rust.
